s1.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation
salient_findings: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding
key_facts: Several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT with contrast
Postseptal fat stranding largely limited to the extraconal space
Increased abscess size with globe compression on follow-up CT
Acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI

shortlist.label: Lacrimal sac abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging studies confirmed left-sided lacrimal sac abscess

shortlist.label: Orbital cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of orbital pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation

shortlist.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of symptoms and absence of clear infectious cause

shortlist.label: Graves' orbitopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Extraocular movement limitation and vision loss, potential autoimmune cause

shortlist.label: Orbital apex syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Vision loss, extraocular movement limitation, and optic nerve injury on MRI

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe vision loss and potential for complications from abscess

shortlist.label: Dacryocystitis

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Painful ophthalmoplegia and potential for inflammatory cause

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of left orbital pain, epiphora, and imaging studies showing a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding and opacification of both nasolacrimal ducts are consistent with a lacrimal sac abscess. The isolation of Streptococcus pyogenes from initial cultures further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: While the patient has signs of orbital inflammation, the specific finding of a lacrimal sac abscess on imaging studies makes this a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
rejected.why: The presence of a lacrimal sac abscess and positive cultures suggest an infectious cause rather than an idiopathic inflammatory process.

rejected.label: Graves' orbitopathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of thyroid disease or other characteristic findings of Graves' orbitopathy, such as proptosis or extraocular muscle involvement.

rejected.label: Orbital apex syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings do not suggest involvement of the orbital apex, and there is no mention of cranial nerve deficits or other characteristic features of this syndrome.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of cavernous sinus involvement on imaging studies, and the patient's symptoms are more localized to the orbit.

rejected.label: Dacryocystitis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of epiphora, the presence of a lacrimal sac abscess and other orbital findings suggest a more complex process than simple dacryocystitis.

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome typically presents with painful ophthalmoplegia and is associated with inflammation of the cavernous sinus or superior orbital fissure, which is not seen in this patient's imaging studies.
